executive_summary: AUD/USD closed at 0.69554 on 2026-10-02, one session after the valuation date. The pair is quoted in US dollars per Australian dollar, so a rising pair means a stronger AUD. It is down 3.41% over one month, up 0.38% over three months, down 1.81% over six months and up 6.81% over a year. Spot sits at the 62nd percentile of its 52-week closing range, below the 50-day (0.70913), 100-day (0.70582) and 200-day (0.70303) averages. The pair lost both 0.7000 and the 200-day on 29 September, the day the RBA hiked. The core bilateral story is two central banks hiking at the same time. The RBA's 4.60% sits 72.5bp above the Fed's 3.875% midpoint, which makes this the only G10 pair where the base currency out-yields the dollar. But the gap is worth almost nothing to a holder: carry divided by three-month implied vol is 0.093, about four pips a month, so AUD is the higher-yielding leg but the yield does not pay for holding it. The two standalone dossiers are both tactically bullish on their own currency (AUD +0.3040, USD +0.3782), so for the pair they largely cancel. Strategically, a naive reading of 'AUD Neutral against USD Bearish' would say buy the pair. That reading falls apart once Australia's 3.67%-of-GDP current account deficit and its real effective exchange rate of 116.11 are netted against the dollar's own twin deficits. The settled verdict is Neutral at conviction 2 on both horizons: tactical score −0.0736 and strategic +0.0929, the latter only 0.0071 below the Bullish threshold. The one datable mispricing is the 3 November RBA meeting. A hike there is priced at roughly a quarter to a third, against a Board that kept the option open, and the Q3 CPI lands on 28 October, the same day as the FOMC. Until that resolves, the working range runs from the seven-touch 0.68707–0.69198 support zone to the three-touch 0.7054–0.7111 resistance zone. The main caveat: CFTC data released after the verdict show the legacy speculative short deepening to −63.2K. That deepens the squeeze-or-breakdown question at the bottom of the range rather than settling it.

market_context.valuation_assessment: The two valuation lenses disagree, and that disagreement is part of the pair's character. Purchasing power parity says modestly cheap: the base dossier's World Bank PPP conversion puts AUD/USD fair value at 0.71483 (flagged as unverified at its own data gate), so spot is 2.7% cheap, the only major AUD cross where AUD is not expensive on PPP. Real exchange rates say rich: AUD's BIS REER is 116.11, up 9.97% over twelve months and the highest in the G10+SGD set, while the dollar's REER of 106.70 sits at the 9th percentile of its post-2024 range. The USD dossier's relative-REER proxy implies AUD/USD near 0.6369, but it divides index levels with different bases, so it is not a fair-value estimate and is reported only to show how far the methods diverge. What the current level prices is the rate differential and nothing else. The REER rose nearly 10% while iron ore, about 35% of Australian export revenue, fell 7.14%. In other words, the market has swapped the terms-of-trade anchor for the carry anchor. That is valuable while the RBA's hiking option is alive and fragile once it is not. On closes the 52-week range is 0.64551 to 0.72584, with spot at the 62nd percentile on both intraday and closing measures.

market_context.recent_regime: September was a dollar-led selloff, not an Australian one. The pair fell from a 0.72193 close on 7 September to 0.69311 on 1 October, a drop of 288 pips. The heaviest sessions were the 16 September FOMC hike, 23 September (−75 pips) and the 29 September RBA hike itself. On that day the pair closed below 0.7000 and the 200-day even though the RBA delivered. Commentary at the time attributed this to the hike being fully priced and to Bullock declining to pre-commit. One account noted that at the press conference Bullock said monetary policy could be restrictive enough to bring inflation back to target, and that markets had priced a cash rate above 5% by May 2027, more than Bullock was willing to signal. The regime is now a test of whether the seven-touch 0.687–0.692 zone holds into the 28 October CPI. The 2 October rebound from 0.69132 to 0.69555 is the first sign it might.

bilateral_carry_analysis.breakeven_move: On the 72.5bp policy differential a long accrues about 4.2 pips a month (0.725% × 0.69554 ÷ 12); on the realised roll about 3.3 pips. Spot can slip only from 0.69554 to roughly 0.6951 in a month before carry is erased, a tenth of one 47-pip ATR. Over six months the cushion is about 25 pips on the policy differential and 19.5 pips on the realised roll.
bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The policy differential is +72.5bp: RBA 4.60% (as of 2026-10-01) against the Fed's 3.875% midpoint (as of 2026-09-28). This is the only G10 dollar pair where a long position earns rather than pays carry. But the CME calendar roll premium (6AV6 to 6AX6, observed 2026-09-30) is −56.2bp annualised, which is what a rolled futures position actually earns; the roughly 16bp gap to the policy differential is negative cross-currency basis, which cannot be separated from the rate component without an OIS curve. Carry-to-vol is 0.093 against the gated 3-month implied of 7.813%, or 0.113 against 60-day realised of 6.39%; both are among the weakest in the AUD complex. Forward points are derived from the CME roll premium applied to the payload spot (no live dealer points). Carry is a ranking signal and not a return engine: it identifies AUD as the highest-yielding G10 currency, but it pays too little per unit of volatility to justify holding this pair for carry. The differential matters to AUD/USD only through repricing of the two front ends (the 3 November RBA option and the 9 December Fed projections round), not through accrual.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: AUD is the only G10 currency that out-yields the dollar: the RBA cash rate of 4.60 per cent sits 72.5bp above the 3.875 per cent Fed midpoint in the gated payload, and the payload's long-end differential is +33.5bp on the monthly August vintage, though both dossiers' live cross-section puts the AU-US 10-year gap nearer +14bp, so the long end has compressed hard while the policy gap has not. The direction of travel over the tactical window is asymmetric in the pair's favour on pricing rather than on level: ASX-implied pricing puts a 3 November RBA hike at roughly a quarter, against a Board that has just hiked unanimously and explicitly retained the option of raising further, while the 28 October FOMC is priced near a coin flip after Williams removed the urgency and the December path matches the dots to within a handful of basis points. The sequencing matters and is datable from the gated calendar: the Fed decides on 2026-10-28 and the RBA on 2026-11-03, so the dollar leg reprices first and the Australian leg carries the later, less-priced event. Transmission into the pair is through the front-end spread rather than through carry, because carry here is close to worthless: 72.5bp against a 3-month ATM implied volatility of 7.813 per cent is a carry-to-vol ratio of 0.093, and the CME calendar premium of -56.2bp annualised says a rolled long AUD position actually realises about 56bp a year once the cross-currency basis is taken out. The stance is Bullish but only at 52 because the level of the differential is static, both central banks are tightening into the same energy shock, and the long-end spread is moving against the base leg.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the question is the direction of the differential, and it tilts marginally toward the base leg. The Fed's September projections put the funds rate at 4.1 per cent at end-2026 and 4.1 per cent at end-2027, which is a committee describing itself as one step from a plateau, while the RBA has anchored its reaction function to a fuel shock it has called permanently higher and has four hikes delivered in 2026 behind it. If the Fed delivers its final step at the 2026-12-09 meeting with the SEP and then holds, while the RBA adds one more at 2026-11-03 or 2026-12-08, the differential widens from 72.5bp toward roughly 97.5bp; if neither moves, it is unchanged. The counterweight is that the pair's rate advantage is not monetisable at this volatility: a carry-to-vol of 0.093 means the differential contributes about six pips a month of cushion, so the factor works only through expectations, not accrual. The Australian front end is already priced flatter than the cash rate implies, and the US long end is carrying a term premium that keeps real yields high, which is why the long-end spread has compressed to roughly nothing even as the policy gap held. Bullish at 52 is the honest reading: the base leg has the higher rate and the live hiking option, the quote leg has the flatter forward path, and the gap between those two facts is thin.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential favours the base leg and the growth differential favours the quote leg, and over four weeks the growth side is the one with momentum. Australian headline monthly CPI has re-accelerated to 4.0 per cent with trimmed mean stuck at 3.6 per cent for three months, against US core PCE of 3.0 per cent and core CPI of 2.4 per cent, so the inflation gap argues for more RBA tightening than Fed tightening. But the activity gap runs the other way and is widening: US Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2 per cent annualised with payrolls at 162,000 against a 55,000 consensus, ISM manufacturing at 54.5 and a flash composite at 58.4, while Australia's composite PMI fell to 50.8 with manufacturing at 49.3, unemployment reached a post-COVID high of 4.6 per cent against a steady US 4.1 per cent, and NAB business conditions turned negative at -2 for the first time since September 2020. Both economies print GDP near 2.1 per cent year on year, so the level of growth is not the differentiator - the second derivative is. Transmission to the pair is through relative data surprise into the two front ends, and the asymmetric sensitivity is on the base leg: Australia's quarterly CPI on 28 October compresses three months into one number six days before the RBA, while the US gets a monthly CPI on 14 October that is already well discounted. Bearish at 55 because the momentum differential is clear while the inflation differential is partially offset by the fact that Australian inflation is cost-push with wages at 3.2 per cent and real wages falling for a third quarter.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices Australia as a sticky-inflation economy that can stop and the US as a resilient one that will not have to, which is roughly where the data sit; the unpriced risk is an Australian Q3 trimmed mean at or above 3.7 per cent on 28 October.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the mix turns stagflationary on the base side and soft-landing on the quote side, which is the configuration in which the pair underperforms its rate differential. Australia's cost shock is compressing margins rather than passing through, with NAB purchase costs up 1.2 per cent in the quarter against final prices of 0.5 per cent, and the labour market is loosening by composition, with the entire August employment gain part-time and full-time down 6,000. The United States is slowing from a higher base - GDPNow has fallen from 5.1 to 3.7 per cent - but core PCE has already eased from 3.3 to 3.0 per cent with unemployment flat at 4.1 per cent, which is disinflation without a demand break. The offset, and the reason confidence is only 50, is that the same US disinflation removes the Fed's need to tighten further, which is the mechanism that eventually narrows the dollar's real-yield premium and supports the pair. Mechanically the two effects race each other: Australian labour-market deterioration pulls the pair down through the rate channel, US core disinflation pushes it up through the same channel. We score the base leg's deterioration as the faster of the two over the window because the Australian unemployment trajectory is already in train and the US inflation fade is a projection.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a moderate risk-proxy pair rather than a pure one: the base leg has the highest risk beta in the G10 through its China and commodity linkage, while the quote leg is mildly counter-cyclical, with the dollar's measured 60-day correlation to the S&P 500 at -0.31 and to the 10-year yield at +0.32. The current configuration is the unfavourable one for the pair - equity volatility is benign, with the VIX in the 16s at the 28th to 34th percentile of its year, but credit has already repriced, with US high yield at 324bp at the 98th percentile of its one-year range and investment grade at 86bp at the 94th. That is a rates-and-credit stress with equities intact, which is precisely the right-hand side of the dollar smile where the quote leg attracts capital on a 2.88 per cent 10-year TIPS yield and the base leg gets no help from its own carry. The China channel, which is the pair's distinctive transmission mechanism, is weak: NBS manufacturing at 50.1 is one month above the line after two below, and Q2 GDP of 4.3 per cent was the slowest since the end of 2022. Bearish at 52 rather than higher because equity resilience and tight absolute credit spreads keep the risk regime from being actively hostile, and because super-fund rebalancing provides a mechanical bid for the base currency while global equities hold their gains.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the risk distribution for this pair is genuinely two-sided because the Gulf binary moves the two legs through offsetting channels. A negotiated Hormuz reopening collapses the energy premium, which is risk-positive and China-growth-positive for the base leg but also removes the supply-shock foundation of the RBA's hiking bias, while simultaneously taking away the quote leg's terms-of-trade gain and part of its haven bid - the net is close to a wash with a mild upward tilt for the pair. A renewed closure reverses both signs, adding to the base leg's rate case while triggering the risk-off in which it has the highest G10 beta. Credit is the second axis and is less symmetric: high yield at 324bp is only the 72nd percentile of five years, so the September widening is a repricing rather than a crisis, and a move toward 450bp would be a left-side funding event that favours the quote leg decisively. The China policy calendar is the one clean upward input for the pair over the window, through the iron ore channel, but it sits mostly at the far end. Neutral at 50 is the honest output: the tails are fat on both sides and roughly balanced, and manufacturing a direction from them would be exactly the kind of thin-evidence stance this pass exists to avoid.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the rare pair where the futures contract is the pair itself, so CFTC data are a direct read rather than a triangulation - and the direct read is self-contradictory. For the same 22 September report date, the legacy non-commercial measure shows a net short of 46,814 contracts that has deepened in each of the last three weeks, while the disaggregated file shows leveraged funds net long 58,726 and asset managers net short 55,353. One says the squeeze fuel for a higher pair is in place; the other says the fast money is already long it. On the quote side, speculators rebuilt an aggregate dollar long to 18.4bn dollars in the week to 22 September, a 12.5bn build that is the fastest in seven years but still only the 44th percentile of the cached range, so the dollar is fresh rather than crowded. Netting the two legs: a moderately short base leg against a mid-range long quote leg gives an amplified but low-confidence downward bias that the leveraged-fund series directly contradicts. Engagement has also collapsed, with AUD open interest down 37.8 per cent in a week to 306,488, which lowers the amplitude of any squeeze in either direction. The one unambiguous structural flow is upward for the pair: nearly nine in ten surveyed Australian superannuation funds intend to raise FX hedge ratios, which mechanically converts offshore equity gains into base-currency demand. Neutral at 50 is the only defensible output when the level of speculative exposure in the pair's own contract cannot be established.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months the speculative layer tells us nothing about the pair because it can be rebuilt several times inside the window and because its level is disputed by the two CFTC report families. What is identifiable is the structural layer, and it points in both directions. Downward for the pair: the dollar's reserve share fell to 56.70 per cent in Q2 from 57.18 per cent while the euro gained, which is a slow diversification away from the quote leg and therefore upward for the pair, but private foreigners were net sellers of US long-term securities in July with official buyers and bills carrying the inflow, which is a financing profile that argues the dollar's holders are shortening duration rather than leaving. Upward for the pair: Australian superannuation hedging is a persistent mechanical bid for the base currency, and Australian hedge ratios are rising from a base where listed equities are only about half hedged. Against that, Australia's net foreign debt of 1,486bn dollars and the structural offshore funding of its banks create a standing dollar demand that works the other way. Neutral at 48 reflects that these flows are real, slow and genuinely offsetting, and that the pair-level speculative read is unusable.

net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Applying the framework direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: mildly positive for the base leg through the coal and LNG substitution channel, but now clearly positive for the quote leg because the United States is a net energy exporter and the shock also lifts US real yields - net effect is the pair FALLS. Iron ore up: strongly positive for the base leg, neutral to mildly negative for the quote leg as an importer of steel-intensive goods - net effect is the pair RISES. Gold up: mildly negative for the quote leg - net effect is the pair rises. The configuration actually in train is oil up roughly 50 per cent on the year and iron ore down 7.14 per cent, which is the adverse combination on both counts: the single commodity that drives the base leg hardest is falling while the complex that now helps the quote leg is at a one-year high. That is the mechanical reason the pair's historical commodity support has disappeared even as the base leg's policy rate reached the top of the G10.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Guidance diverges cleanly and in the pair's favour. The RBA hiked unanimously on 29 September, judged that a further tightening in financial conditions is warranted, and retained the option explicitly, with the Governor adding that inflationary pressures will persist longer than expected and that the fuel increase is permanently higher; she also named the exchange rate as the most important channel of transmission, which means the base-leg central bank has no incentive to talk its currency down. The Fed hiked 12-0 with a commitment to deliver price stability, but its own projections describe a plateau at 4.1 per cent through 2027, and a permanent voter removed the urgency from the next meeting. One central bank is guiding toward an option it has not used; the other is guiding toward a stop. The credibility differential is small - both committees are cohesive and both have hiked against political or domestic pressure - so the factor is about direction of guidance rather than about trust. Sequencing from the gated calendar sharpens it: the Fed decides on 2026-10-28 with no projection round flagged, and the RBA follows on 2026-11-03, so the base leg has the last word inside the tactical window. Bullish at 58, which is the highest confidence on any factor here, because the gap between a stated hiking option and a quarter of it being priced is measurable rather than inferred.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Inside four weeks the event set is dense and close to symmetric for this pair. The Hormuz binary is the largest single item and it cuts across the two legs rather than between them: a settlement is risk-positive and China-growth-positive for the base leg but removes the supply-shock foundation of its central bank's hiking bias, while also stripping the quote leg of its energy terms-of-trade gain and part of its haven bid. The residual channel specific to this pair is US-China trade policy, which transmits to the base leg through steel and iron ore demand faster than to any other G10 currency. tactical.bilateral_analysis: Dollar funding is abundant and the dollar is strong anyway, which is the configuration that hurts this pair most. The plumbing is unstressed: SOFR fixed at 3.87 per cent against an IORB of 3.90 and a standing repo rate of 4.00, reserves are 2.948tn dollars, runoff ended in December 2025 and the Desk is adding bills at ten billion a month. But ample liquidity is not a weak dollar - the ten-year TIPS real yield of 2.88 per cent sits at the 99th percentile of its year, which places the quote leg at the US-exceptionalism end of the dollar smile, the end at which this base currency has the highest beta to underperformance of anything in the G10. The pair-specific funding read is in the gated store: a CME calendar premium of -56.2bp annualised against a 72.5bp policy differential implies roughly sixteen basis points of negative basis, a modest dollar funding premium that the base leg pays rather than receives. Australia's banks are structural net offshore borrowers in dollars, so any tightening in that basis transmits directly into the pair rather than being absorbed. Bearish at 55 with the heaviest tactical weight after the top two factors.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to three months this factor is a genuine standoff for the pair, which is the unusual case where both legs' own dossiers score the same factor as a headwind for their own currency. On the quote side, the Fed's operating framework is designed to prevent the dollar shortage that would support the currency - reserves are ample at 2.948tn, the standing repo facility caps any spike, the balance sheet is growing and the Committee has committed to keeping reserves ample - and peer tightening lowers the cost for foreign holders of US assets to raise hedge ratios, which is a slow dollar-selling flow. Neither effect dominates. Neutral at 50 is the honest reading, and it is worth noting that scoring this factor Bullish at even 48 would push the strategic net score across the Bullish threshold - which is exactly why the judgement has to be made on the evidence rather than on where it lands.

tactical.score_interpretation: A net score of -0.0736 falls inside the -0.10 to +0.10 band, so the derived tactical stance is Neutral with a mild downward tilt. The structure is a standoff rather than an absence of information: the two largest positive contributions, Policy and Rates at +0.1248 and Guidance at +0.0406, are produced by the same underlying fact - a base-leg central bank holding an open hiking option that the market discounts at roughly a quarter - while the four negatives are produced by a different and equally coherent fact, namely that the quote leg currently sits at the high-real-rate end of the dollar smile with better growth momentum, a credit tape that favours it and an option surface that pays for downside in the pair. tactical.rationale: At tactical weights the verdict is decided by Policy and Rates at 0.24, Inflation and Growth at 0.18 and USD Liquidity at 0.11, which together carry 53 per cent of the score and split two to one against the pair. The single bilateral fact that supports a long is that this is the only G10 pair where the base currency out-yields the dollar, by 72.5bp on policy, and where the base-leg central bank has just hiked unanimously and explicitly kept the option of doing more while ASX pricing discounts roughly a quarter of a move at the 2026-11-03 decision. The facts against it are that the differential does not pay - a 0.093 carry-to-vol on a 7.813 per cent three-month implied means the gap contributes about six pips a month - that the long-end spread has compressed to roughly fourteen basis points on the live cross-section, that growth momentum is decisively on the quote side with a flash composite at 58.4 against 50.8, and that the pair's own option surface pays -1.283 per cent at the 25-delta for downside protection at the front of the curve. The two dossiers reinforce rather than conflict in an awkward way: both are tactically bullish their own currency, at +0.3040 and +0.3782, and the pair is simply the smaller of the two numbers subtracted from the larger. What is priced and what we expect diverge in exactly one measurable place - the base-leg hike probability for 3 November, which sits near a quarter against a Board that has used the word further - and the offsetting unpriced item is the quote leg's growth and real-yield momentum into its own 2026-10-28 decision. The dated sequence that resolves it is tight and asymmetric: the US September CPI on 14 October, the Australian labour force report on 15 October, the Australian Q3 CPI on 28 October, the FOMC the same day and the base-leg decision on 3 November, which also happens to be the day of the US midterms. The path of least resistance inside four weeks is sideways with a downward tilt: the pair has one dated upward catalyst on 28 October to 3 November and a continuous downward drag from relative growth and real yields in between. Conviction is 2 rather than 3 because the whole positive case is one release wide, because the pair's own positioning data contradict themselves at the contract level, and because a Neutral arrived at by subtracting two confident bullish views is less informative than a Neutral arrived at from agreement. Analyst note on the verdict (pass 2): information arriving after pass 1 points both ways and does not argue for a different score. It supports the AUD-positive factors (1 and 6): Westpac has moved to a November hike call (Westpac still expects another RBA rate hike in November), and Bullock has also been reported as saying that three RBA hikes could tame inflation toward target. It supports the AUD-negative factor (2): over the same days, consumer sentiment fell 4.7% to 80.4 in October, and dropped to 67.2 among those surveyed after the RBA hike, a level previously seen only in the early 1990s recession. Where I disagree: if anything, the scenario set gives the downside tail more width than a symmetric reading of a −0.07 score implies. That reflects the deepening CFTC short and the persistent put skew. It is a judgement about levels and tails, not about direction, and the scored verdict stands as issued.
tactical.g10_relative_ranking: Within the AUD complex this is the weakest available expression of the base leg's rate advantage: 72.5bp on a 0.093 carry-to-vol ranks behind AUD/CHF, AUD/SEK, AUD/CAD and EUR/AUD, all of which pay two to six times the differential per unit of volatility. Within the USD complex the pair is the best-funded short-dollar expression precisely because it is the only G10 pair where the dollar pays rather than receives carry, which makes it a poor long and an expensive short; dollar bears are better served against JPY, where the valuation gap and the peer hiking cycle are both larger. Ranked across the eleven-currency opportunity set the pair sits mid-table tactically, behind outright long-dollar expressions against CHF, EUR and CAD and behind long-AUD expressions against the low-rate funders.

strategic.score_interpretation: A net score of +0.0929 is Neutral by the stated rule, but it is only 0.0071 from the Bullish threshold and the proximity should be stated plainly rather than smoothed over. Five factors are positive and three negative, so breadth is doing real work here: Policy and Rates at +0.1248 is the largest single contribution, but Guidance at +0.0624, Fiscal at +0.0385 and Event Risk at +0.0250 together exceed it, which means the upward tilt rests on a cluster of individually weak, slow-acting institutional advantages on the base leg rather than on one strong driver. Against them, External Balance at -0.0928 is the single heaviest negative and the best-evidenced factor in the set. Two single changes would tip the score Bullish: Factor 10 turning Bullish at even 48 confidence, or Factor 2 softening to Neutral. Equally, External Balance scored five points of confidence higher would hold it Neutral. A score this close to a boundary is a statement that the pair is genuinely balanced over a quarter, not that it is quietly bullish.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the composition changes completely: External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.16, Guidance from 0.07 to 0.12 and Fiscal from 0.04 to 0.07, while Inflation and Growth falls from 0.18 to 0.10 - and the result is a weighted score of +0.0929, a genuine standoff. The upward case is institutional and slow: the base leg has the higher policy rate with a live option, a central bank that has anchored its reaction function to a shock it has called permanent, triple-A ratings against a quote leg one notch down with debt at 101 per cent of GDP and a funding deadline on 2026-12-11, and an event calendar whose dated risks sit almost entirely on the quote side. The downward case is arithmetic and better evidenced: the base leg's current-account deficit widened to 3.67 per cent of GDP with the goods and services balance itself in deficit, its real effective exchange rate is 116.11 and up 9.97 per cent over twelve months - the largest real appreciation in the G10 set - and it achieved that while iron ore, roughly thirty-five per cent of its export revenue, fell 7.14 per cent. The bilateral trade relationship adds a small standing drag: Australia runs a 19.9bn dollar goods deficit with the United States on IMF DOTS for 2024. The two dossiers conflict here in a way the tactical horizon hid: the base dossier is strategically Neutral at +0.0307 while the quote dossier is strategically Bearish at -0.1822, which taken naively would make the pair a clear buy, but the bilateral netting removes most of that because the quote leg's two biggest strategic negatives - a twin deficit and a diversifying reserve share - have direct base-leg analogues that are worse per unit of GDP. What is priced is the differential staying at 72.5bp and neither external position adjusting; what we expect is that the base leg's hiking option survives slightly longer than the market credits while its real exchange rate does not. The dated resolution points inside the window are the 2026-11-03 and 2026-12-08 base-leg decisions, the 2026-12-09 FOMC SEP - the only flagged projection round in the gated calendar - and the 2026-12-11 US funding deadline. Conviction is 2 because the offsetting factors are large, well identified and slow, and because a score 0.0071 from a threshold is not a position.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically the pair ranks mid-table and is the wrong vehicle for either side of the view it contains. A strategic long in the base leg is better expressed against the low-rate funders, where the differential is 210 to 460 basis points rather than 72.5 and survives a seven per cent volatility environment; a strategic short in the quote leg is better expressed against JPY, where the valuation gap and the peer tightening cycle are both far larger and the option skew already pays for it. Among dollar pairs AUD/USD is the only one where the dollar pays carry, which flatters a long and penalises a short; among AUD crosses it is the one with no commodity support underneath it, because the quote leg is now a net energy exporter too.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Consensus is built almost entirely on one factor - that Australian rates stay above US rates for longer - and that factor is both real and almost unmonetisable at current volatility: 72.5bp against a 7.813 per cent three-month implied is a carry-to-vol of 0.093, roughly six pips a month, and the realised roll in the gated store is 56.2bp rather than 72.5bp once basis is removed. Second, relative valuation: a real effective exchange rate at 116.11 and up 9.97 per cent over twelve months against a quote leg at the 9th percentile of its own recent range, achieved while iron ore fell 7.14 per cent, which means the rate story is already capitalised and has no commodity support underneath it. consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: If the consensus is right and the Australian hiking cycle extends into 2027 while the Fed's plateau proves real, the pair appreciates through the bank range and a Neutral verdict forgoes it. cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The two horizons agree on the label and disagree on the sign of the tilt, which is worth stating rather than hiding behind the shared word Neutral. Tactically the score is mildly negative because the heavily weighted growth and funding factors favour the quote leg while the base leg's rate advantage is unmonetisable; strategically the score is mildly positive because External Balance rises to 0.16 and hurts the base leg, but Guidance, Fiscal and Event Risk rise together and all three favour it, and the quote leg's funding advantage decays into Neutral. Nothing about either currency changes between the horizons - what changes is which of their contradictory properties carries the weight. The composition is also different in kind: the tactical tilt rests on two well-evidenced factors, while the strategic tilt rests on four individually weak ones, which is breadth doing the work of depth.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The window between the 2026-11-03 base-leg decision and the 2026-12-09 FOMC with its SEP. The first resolves whether the base leg's open hiking option is used; the second resolves whether the quote leg's plateau is confirmed or extended. Once both are known, the tactical drag and the strategic tilt stop pointing in opposite directions.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: A Neutral on both horizons with opposite tilts is an instruction to hold no directional position in this pair and to let the second pass express the view, if at all, through relative value rather than outright spot. The one genuinely datable asymmetry - the base-leg hike option discounted at roughly a quarter into 2026-11-03 - is a short-duration event exposure, not a trend, and the option surface says near-dated optionality in this pair is not yet bid up relative to the rest of its curve.

This release decides whether 5.0% unemployment arrives inside the strategic window. At that level Factors 1 and 6, which carry 0.36 of strategic weight, lose their support together. That is the fastest route from Neutral to Bearish.
If November delivered, this is the hold that defines the peak. If November held, this becomes the live meeting with October and November data in hand.

assumptions: Price series: the price payload delivered dataPoints = 130 weekday bars with dateRange '2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02'. spot = 0.69554 at spotDate 2026-10-02. Averages and zones are computed over computationRange '2007-12-24 to 2026-10-02 (4900 weekday bars)'. The payload's dataQuality lines: 'AUD/USD: only 2 resistance / 9 support zones met the 2-touch threshold — supplement with round numbers and note the shortfall' and 'AUD/USD: 4900 weekday bars in the store (2007-12-24 to 2026-10-02); 1007 weekly, 500 monthly; 130 daily bars passed downstream (2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02), which is the 1-6 month strategic horizon'.

Spot anchoring and the date gap: spotDate is one session after the 2026-10-01 valuation date. Every level, pip distance, percentage and target is anchored to 0.69554. Later web quotes, such as AUD/USD rising 0.37% to 0.6972 on 5 October, are noted but not used. The resistance shortfall flagged in the data-quality note is filled with round-number and 52-week-high reference levels, labelled as such and carrying no touch count.

Moving averages: all are simple averages of trading-day closes. The 200-week slope of +0.000278 a week is taken from the payload. The end-March projection of about 0.6730 is linear arithmetic (26 weeks × 0.000278 added to 0.66574), not a forecast.

The scored verdict: factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weights, rationales and both synthesis blocks are carried verbatim from pass 1, which scored them without price data. Pass-2 notes appended to Factor 4, Factor 9, the tactical synthesis and the consensus section are labelled and do not alter any score. Default weights are applied on both horizons.

Forward points: derived from the gated CME calendar roll premium (−56.2bp annualised, 6AV6 to 6AX6, observed 2026-09-30). By covered interest parity that figure bundles the interest differential with the cross-currency basis. No live dealer forward points were used.

Volatility: implied volatility, risk reversals and butterflies are the payload's CME values observed 2026-09-30. The '3M' figure is measured at 99.7 days, not 90. A one-year implied-vol percentile is not computable because the cached history begins 2026-08-21 (iv_percentile is therefore null). One-standard-deviation ranges use ATM implied scaled by the square root of tenor over 365.

Yields and differentials: the payload's 10-year yields are monthly vintages as of 2026-08-01 and are not quoted as live levels. Live spread references use the dossiers' late-September cross-sections. The AU-US 2-year spread of about +20bp combines the AUD dossier's 2-year of 4.98% and the USD dossier's 4.78%, from slightly different dates.

Positioning: the CFTC legacy figure of −63.2K comes from a calendar aggregator's 2 October release and has not been reconciled against the disaggregated file. The pass-1 contradiction between the legacy and disaggregated series remains unresolved.

Scenarios and expected values: scenario probabilities are this pass's own assessments and sum to 100% on each horizon. Expected values are stated for a long from 0.69554 and exclude transaction costs. Position-sizing figures are illustrative.
Market pricing for 3 November: estimates range from about 20% (base dossier) through 24.8% (ASX tracker) to 33% (Admiral Markets). No conclusion depends on resolving that range.
Data provenance: dossier data are referenced without re-citation. Citations 1–30 are pass-1 sources carried with the verbatim factors. Citations 31–46 were accessed during this pass.
